conclusion: Historical benchmark only, at the checkout and host recorded in the durable evidence: For the recorded large Benchy on the measured 16-core Windows host, the latest support-corrected baseline takes 43.542s median over three trials; a local contact-collision reuse candidate takes 42.654s with strongly overlapping ranges, so the experiment does not establish a stable substantial total speedup or halving. Sampled CPU medians fall from 300.641 to 292.516s and initial sampling medians from 7.092 to 5.008s. All 811657 ordered printer commands, motion role/width/height annotations and emitted configuration remain identical. Initial sampling mostly spends its worker elapsed time in roof and regular component geometry/line generation. Keep reuse local to a fixed batch/layer; changing a value-returning contact arm into a separate branch also prevents copies of ordinary reference-returning avoidance polygons. Further speed work needs complete-key geometry/fill reuse and profiling of support assembly, toolpaths and non-support stages, without changing deterministic publication or contact rules. These timings and command identities do not describe the current endpoint-fix build and must be remeasured before any current performance claim.
scope: Historical 2026-10-16 Benchy benchmark, not current-build performance or path identity.
